checks.name: a file backs what it said it delivered

must.why: Jet looks like a hybrid F-18/F-22/F-35 with a pointed nose, tall upright tail fins, and a single-seat canopy. The tails are not clearly canted, and the exhaust is not clearly a single F-35 nozzle. It resembles an F/A-18 more than an F-35.
Frame 1 shows the jet rolling on the runway with its gear down. Frame 2 shows it airborne just after lift-off.

must.item: Consistent aircraft design between runway and airborne
must.why: Two tails show in frames 1-2 and the shape differs from frames 3-4. In frame 3 only one tail is visible, and the fuselage and intakes change slightly.

must.item: All three labels appear exactly and legible
must.why: No on-screen text appears in any of the four sampled frames.

must.item: Audible English narration on one engine and conventional takeoff
must.why: The audio has sound, but the spoken words were not transcribed.

faults.what: All requested on-screen labels are missing from the sampled frames.
The jet shape is not a faithful F-35: it has a pointed nose, upright F-18-style tails, and looks like a hybrid.
The airframe changes between the runway and airborne shots. The tail count and fuselage look different.
The second half is not clearly above the clouds. It is a low sky view with the jet near cloud level.

summary: The clip shows a realistic-looking jet rolling and taking off, then flying. It has no on-screen text at all, and the jet reads as an F-18/F-22 hybrid rather than a true F-35A.
